name: Canyon_Strata_Visuals
description: The visible rock layers in the canyon walls — color, texture, and stratification patterns that let players identify rock types by sight

questions.question: Can the player visually distinguish between different rock strata types (sedimentary vs igneous layers) at a glance?
Would a close-up screenshot of stratified canyon walls showing distinct color bands be visually striking enough for Steam marketing?
Do strata layers have realistic thickness variation, color transitions, and erosion patterns that make the canyon feel geologically ancient?
Can strata materials be authored using existing UE5 landscape layer blends and material instances without requiring custom HLSL shaders?
Does strata visualization reuse the existing splat-rendering pipeline in core/matter_gpu.py, or does it require new rendering infrastructure?
Are strata layer materials compatible with UE5.8s virtual texture system without requiring workarounds for layer count limits?
Do strata visual layers fit within a draw-call budget of 200 or fewer per canyon vista at medium distance?
Is there a pattern-overlay or tooltip alternative so colorblind players can still distinguish strata layers?
Does each rock type in the strata layer produce a distinct footstep or tool-impact audio response when the player walks across or mines it?
Are strata visual layers deterministic and consistent across all clients when multiple players view the same canyon wall section?
Can community members add new rock-type materials and strata color palettes through data-driven configs without recompiling?
Are rock-type display names, stratum layer labels, and educational identifiers stored in localization tables for translation?
Does strata visuals depend on a completed geology data model (rock type definitions, layer ordering, color maps) before materials can be authored?
Does rendering visually distinct strata prove that the procedural canyon generator produces geologically meaningful layered output?
Is strata visualization derived from the educational requirement that players identify rock types by observable visual features?
Do high-detail strata textures with 4+ material layers conflict with the performance budget for real-time camera flythroughs?
What material-editor and texture-pipeline knowledge is needed to author strata layer blends that look geologically plausible?
Do visually distinct strata layers directly serve the seed goal of teaching real geology through pure environmental observation?
What visual fidelity is sacrificed if strata layers use only 2 material layer blends instead of 4?
How do we know that players can actually learn to identify rock types from visual strata alone rather than needing a UI label?
Does the observation chain strata visible to player identifies rock -> player learns geology reach a human learner without requiring an intermediate LLM?
Does strata visuals need deeper sub-features (fossil layer markers, specific erosion textures per rock type) or is it sufficient at current granularity?
Are sibling visual features missing at this level such as a strata-legend UI overlay or a strata-comparison tool?
Is Demo_Canyon_Terrain already detailed enough about visual layering to support this sub-feature without reopening parent questions?
Should strata visuals be built before or after terrain generation given that strata render onto generated geometry?
Does incomplete strata visualization block any other canyon features or do other features depend on strata being visible first?
